findings.problem: At the end of [2:205], Holmes has said only that Clay used a red-haired accomplice, that 'one rogue' kept the office while 'the other' urged Wilson to apply, and that the assistant had a strong motive. Three things in the snapshots come later. The cellar tunnel is reasoned out at [2:207]. The link to the bank is made at [2:208]. The text never names the assistant as Clay outright: it builds that through [2:207] ('this mysterious assistant… one of the coolest and most daring criminals') and [2:208] ('We have had some skirmishes'), echoing [2:204]. Both snapshots (Vincent's 'dig a tunnel from the cellar to the bank'; Clay's 'under the name Vincent Spaulding') are therefore a few paragraphs early.
findings.evidence: [2:207] 'I could think of nothing save that he was running a tunnel to some other building.' / [2:208] 'I walked round the corner, saw the City and Suburban Bank abutted on our friend’s premises, and felt that I had solved my problem.'
findings.fix: Move the gate of the vincent-spaulding '(John Clay)' snapshot and the john-clay [2:205] snapshot from [2:205] to [2:208]. Leave the duncan-ross and archie [2:205] snapshots at [2:205]; their content is supported there.

findings.problem: 'coiner' mistranslates Jones's 'smasher' (a passer of counterfeit coin, not a maker of it). The modern edition itself says 'passer of counterfeit money'.
findings.evidence: [2:169] O: 'John Clay, the murderer, thief, smasher, and forger.' M: 'murderer, thief, passer of counterfeit money, and forger'
findings.fix: Replace 'murderer, thief, coiner and forger' with 'murderer, thief, passer of counterfeit coin and forger'.

findings.problem: The card makes him chairman of directors of the City branch. The text makes him chairman of the bank's directors, and the cellar belongs to the City branch.
findings.evidence: [2:178] 'in the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks. Mr. Merryweather is the chairman of directors' / [2:208] 'the chairman of the bank directors'
findings.fix: Body: 'Chairman of the directors of one of the principal London banks. He leads the party into the cellar of its City branch, where the bank keeps 30,000 French napoleons borrowed from the Bank of France and has had warnings of an attempt on them.'

findings.problem: The first card says he misses his Saturday-night game of cards. He says so only at [2:167].
findings.evidence: [2:167] 'It is the first Saturday night for seven-and-twenty years that I have not had my rubber.'
findings.fix: Delete the final sentence of the [2:163] body ('He misses his Saturday-night game of cards.'). Optionally add a [2:167] snapshot appending: 'He laments missing his Saturday-night game of cards for the first time in twenty-seven years.'

findings.problem: The subtitle says the advertisement calls him the League's founder. The advertisement mentions only his bequest; 'founded' and 'American millionaire' are Spaulding's account at [2:52]. The thread likewise calls him 'the late American millionaire' and credits the advertisement.
findings.evidence: [2:28] 'On account of the bequest of the late Ezekiah Hopkins, of Lebanon, Pennsylvania, U.S.A.' / [2:52] 'As far as I can make out, the League was founded by an American millionaire, Ezekiah Hopkins'
findings.fix: Subtitle: 'Benefactor named in the Red-Headed League’s advertisement'. Thread: 'The late benefactor of Lebanon, Pennsylvania, whose bequest, according to the advertisement, funds the Red-Headed League.'

findings.problem: The thread calls him Wilson's 'capable young assistant'. Wilson explicitly says he is not so young and is nearly thirty.
findings.evidence: [2:35] 'His name is Vincent Spaulding, and he’s not such a youth, either.' / [2:121] 'though he’s not short of thirty'
findings.fix: Thread: 'Wilson’s capable assistant, who works for half wages to learn the trade and spends his spare time on photography. He is the one who shows Wilson the League’s advertisement.'

findings.problem: She is only named in passing here, but the fixed subtitle already carries 'short-sighted' (with typist and Camberwell) from her own story. Her short sight matters to how A Case of Identity resolves, and the subtitle is fixed, so it is shown before Holmes points it out in story 3. Typist and Camberwell are harmless identity facts.
findings.evidence: [2:9] 'just before we went into the very simple problem presented by Miss Mary Sutherland'
findings.fix: Subtitle: 'Holmes’s client; a typist from Camberwell'. Mention her short sight in a story-3 snapshot body at or after the paragraph where Holmes remarks on it.

findings.problem: At [2:134] Holmes only proposes the concert. Watson agrees at [2:135], and they attend at [2:151].
findings.evidence: [2:134] 'Sarasate plays at the St. James’s Hall this afternoon… Could your patients spare you for a few hours?'
findings.fix: Replace the second sentence with: 'Holmes invites Watson to hear him play at St. James’s Hall.'
